concepts.title: Transaction Manager
concepts.definition: The service that stages immutable candidates, applies them atomically where possible, verifies results, and restores original bytes during rollback.
concepts.thesis: Transaction Manager should make mutation permission deterministic, proportional, exact, and reviewable.

concepts.title: CFEL: Collision, Failure, Evidence, and Learning Feedback
concepts.definition: CFEL records the difference between expectation and observation, blocks unchanged blind retries, and turns failure into bounded evidence for a revised model.
concepts.thesis: A failure is valuable only when it changes the next hypothesis, experiment, or action.

concepts.title: EON: Exact Governed Action Boundary
concepts.definition: EON binds a proposed operation to exact authority, source state, targets, candidate content, commands, tests, invariants, risk, expiry, and use limits.
concepts.thesis: Reasoning should cross into mutation only through an exact, reviewable, stale-detecting action identity.

concepts.title: Evidence Gate
concepts.definition: The evidence gate compares the proposed action's declared requirements with current artifacts, authority, approval, risk, and invariants.
concepts.thesis: The gate should decide from deterministic records rather than from the model's confidence or persuasive language.

concepts.title: Governed Action
concepts.definition: A governed action is the actual mutation or command execution performed only after the exact candidate passes its deterministic gate.
concepts.thesis: Execution should be the consequence of evidence and authority, not a side effect of model reasoning.

concepts.title: HRT: Human-Readable Task Interpretation
concepts.definition: HRT turns a human request into explicit claims, assumptions, ambiguities, scope, exclusions, and provenance before deeper reasoning begins.
concepts.thesis: Human intent should be made inspectable before the system treats it as an engineering problem.

concepts.title: IEPS: Invariant and Evidence Production System
concepts.definition: IEPS produces coverage, oracles, counterexamples, uniqueness checks, mutations, shrinking, qualification, and evidence gates.
concepts.thesis: A candidate should meet evidence designed to discriminate truth from plausible appearance.

concepts.title: IURM: Invariant-Uncertainty-Response Modeling
concepts.definition: IURM identifies dimensions, baselines, controlled variations, interactions, sensitivity, and minimum viable designs.
concepts.thesis: Useful learning comes from discriminating experiments, not from changing many coupled dimensions at once.

concepts.title: OURD: Object-Universe-Relation-Dependency Modeling
concepts.definition: OURD builds the relational map of the problem: objects, boundaries, dependencies, goals, impacts, exclusions, and unresolved relations.
concepts.thesis: The agent should model the territory before choosing one imagined implementation path.

glossary.ADR: Architecture Decision Record: a short document that records a significant design choice, its context, and its consequences.
glossary.API: Application Programming Interface: a defined way for software components to request services from one another.
glossary.C0: Capability class 0: observation only; it may inspect information but cannot create proposals or change the workspace.
glossary.C1: Capability class 1: analysis and internal proposal creation without ordinary workspace mutation.
glossary.C2: Capability class 2: simulation in a disposable, synthetic, or otherwise isolated environment.
glossary.C3: Capability class 3: local workspace mutation through the governed EON execution boundary with exact authority and approval.
glossary.C4: Capability class 4: mutation of an external system; EGCFv1 currently fails closed for this class.
glossary.C5: Capability class 5: critical or destructive mutation; EGCFv1 currently fails closed for this class.
glossary.C0-C5: The full capability-class ladder, from observation-only C0 through critical or destructive C5 operations.
glossary.C2-C5: Capability classes 2 through 5: simulation, local mutation, external mutation, and critical or destructive mutation.
glossary.C3-C5: The mutation-capable classes: governed local mutation, external mutation, and critical or destructive mutation.
glossary.CAD: Computer-Aided Design: software and data used to create or analyse engineered geometry.
glossary.CFEL: Collision, Failure, Evidence, and Learning feedback: the project loop that records meaningful failures and prevents unchanged blind retries.
glossary.CLI: Command-Line Interface: a text-based way to operate software by entering commands.
glossary.DAG: Directed Acyclic Graph: a one-way network with no cycles, often used to represent workflows and dependencies.
glossary.EGCF: Evidence-Governed Command Fabric: the semantic command layer that compiles intent into typed, content-addressed, policy-checked workflow plans.
glossary.EON: Execution and Operational Nexus: the governed boundary that binds authority, evidence, approval, exact targets, commands, and rollback before execution.
glossary.GIF: Graphics Interchange Format: a bitmap image format that can contain simple animation.
glossary.GLB: The binary container form of glTF, used to package 3D scenes and assets into one file.
glossary.GLTF: GL Transmission Format: a standard format for transmitting 3D scenes and models.
glossary.GPU: Graphics Processing Unit: a processor designed for highly parallel work such as graphics and machine-learning calculations.
glossary.GUI: Graphical User Interface: windows, controls, and visual feedback through which a person operates the system.
glossary.HRT: Human-Readable Task interpretation: the project layer that turns a request into explicit claims, assumptions, ambiguities, scope, and provenance.
glossary.HTML: HyperText Markup Language: the structural language used to describe web pages.
glossary.HTTP: Hypertext Transfer Protocol: the request-and-response protocol commonly used by web clients and servers.
glossary.ID: Identifier: a value used to name and distinguish one object from another.
glossary.IEPS: Invariant and Evidence Production System: the project namespace for generating coverage, oracles, counterexamples, mutations, and qualification evidence.
glossary.IURM: Invariant-Uncertainty-Response Modeling: the project method for defining dimensions, baselines, controlled variations, interactions, sensitivity, and minimum viable designs.
glossary.JPEG: Joint Photographic Experts Group image: a compressed bitmap format commonly used for photographs.
glossary.JSON: JavaScript Object Notation: a text format for structured data made from objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null values.
glossary.JSONL: JSON Lines: a log-friendly format with one complete JSON value on each line.
glossary.L0: Evidence or risk level 0: the lowest project level, normally suitable for observation or automatic handling.
glossary.L1: Evidence or risk level 1: a bounded level that requires stronger policy and evidence than simple observation.
glossary.L2: Evidence or risk level 2: a higher-impact level requiring grounded evidence, counterexamples, and explicit human review unless exact authority says otherwise.
glossary.L0-L2: The project evidence or risk ladder from low-impact observation through higher-impact work requiring stronger evidence and review.
glossary.LRU: Least Recently Used: a cache policy that removes the items that have gone unused for the longest time.
glossary.MCP: Model Context Protocol: a protocol for connecting AI applications to tools and structured external context.
glossary.MVD: Minimum Viable Design: the smallest design that still satisfies the declared constraints and learning objective.
glossary.OBJ: Wavefront OBJ: a text-based file format for polygonal 3D geometry.
glossary.OFAT: One Factor At a Time: an experiment strategy that varies one input while holding the others steady.
glossary.OURD: Object-Universe-Relation-Dependency modeling: the project layer that identifies system objects, their boundaries, relations, dependencies, impacts, exclusions, and scope.
glossary.PEP: Python Enhancement Proposal: a design document used to propose and explain changes to Python.
glossary.PLY: Polygon File Format: a format for storing 3D meshes and point-cloud attributes.
glossary.PNG: Portable Network Graphics: a lossless bitmap image format with transparency support.
glossary.PTY: Pseudo-terminal: a software endpoint that behaves like a terminal so another program can control interactive command-line processes.
glossary.RFC: Request for Comments: a published technical specification or best-current-practice document in the Internet standards process.
glossary.SDK: Software Development Kit: libraries, tools, examples, and documentation used to build software against a platform.
glossary.SHA-256: Secure Hash Algorithm 256-bit: a function that produces a fixed-size digest used here to identify and verify exact content.
glossary.SQL: Structured Query Language: a language for storing, querying, and updating relational data.
glossary.SQLite: A compact relational database engine stored in a local file rather than a separate database server.
glossary.SSDF: Secure Software Development Framework: NIST guidance for integrating secure practices into the software lifecycle.
glossary.STL: Stereolithography file format: a widely used representation of triangulated 3D surfaces.
glossary.SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics: XML-based vector artwork that can remain sharp at any size and can be manipulated with JavaScript.
glossary.TCP: Transmission Control Protocol: a reliable ordered transport protocol used by many network applications.
glossary.UI: User Interface: the controls and information through which a person interacts with a system.
glossary.URL: Uniform Resource Locator: the address used to locate a resource such as a web page or file.
glossary.X11: The X Window System protocol commonly used to display graphical Linux applications.
glossary.COUNT: A configuration field that limits or reports how many items are involved.
glossary.KEY: A configuration field or lookup name used to select a value.
glossary.MODEL: A configuration field that names the language or reasoning model to use.
glossary.SECONDS: A duration field measured in seconds.
glossary.TOKENS: A limit expressed in model tokens, which are small units of text processed by a language model.
